beats: Hook (line_qc_min_three_rafts, then the cover): Shor needed nine qubits to protect one; five turn out to be enough, and four can never work, because a four-qubit code would be a copy machine. Rafts of nine, seven (Steane, QC08-07) and five logs each carry the same crate; the crate rides on the raft as a whole, no single log holds it (the information lives in the whole block). Same cast as QC08-05: the keeper (the code) and the imp (the noise).

The five-qubit code (Q25-11 19:23-22:18, clip 19:32-19:57 "the smallest for any single-qubit error"; Q24-11 62:41-63:39, her answer only after the student question at 62:41-63:08): four checks, XZZXI and its cyclic shifts; unlike Shor's checks (each all X or all Z, 21:00-21:40) every check mixes X and Z (line_qc_min_mixed_glasses: QC08-03's round Z lens and square X lens in one frame; reuse line_qc_hbridge_two_glasses). Tape Q24-11 s17.

Check it by program (Q24-11 63:39-64:07, "as a computer scientist, you can write a program"): list the 15 single-qubit errors (X, Y, Z on five qubits), compute which of the four bulbs each one lights (reuse line_qc_catch_four_bulbs), and all 15 patterns must differ. Four bulbs give 16 patterns: 15 errors plus "all dark = no error", every pattern used exactly once (line_qc_min_key_rack; the empty top-left hook is "no error"). FACTS: the quantum Hamming bound 2^(n-k) >= 1 + 3n holds with equality at n = 5 (a perfect code): check before saying "perfect".

Why not four (Q24-11 64:25-66:15, clip 65:22-66:15 "physically equivalent to cloning: it cannot"; tape Q24-11 s18, her slide): fixing one unknown error is as hard as fixing two erasures (known positions), so any two of the four qubits would rebuild the state; split them into two pairs and each pair rebuilds it: a copy machine (line_qc_min_two_pairs; reuse line_qc_cnot_copier_envelope from QC05-04). With five, any split leaves one side with two or fewer qubits: only one side can rebuild. FACTS: quantum Singleton bound n >= 4t + 1.

Knowing more about the noise does better (Q24-11 58:34-59:01). Erasures: knowing where, not what, doubles what a code can fix, 2t erasures instead of t errors; a lost photon is the classic erasure (59:01-59:54) (line_qc_min_choir_gaps; reuse line_qc_hier_hybrid_lab for the photonic table).

Biased noise: hardware where one error type dominates; build the protection on the side the weather comes from (59:54-60:46 names a cloud company's hardware programme: keep it off screen and out of the narration; her "X error much higher than Z" is checked in FACTS before any caption names the type; cat qubits as a neutral research line, cite papers only by author) (line_qc_min_wind_hedge).

Bursts: cosmic-ray events hit many qubits of a large superconducting chip at once, and knowing when one happened helps the decoder (61:14-62:08; McEwen et al., Nature Physics 2022) (line_qc_min_hail_patch).
Close on her line (clip Q24-11 62:08-62:41): in real applications you can do much more: the beauty of research.

Cover (line_qc_cover_08_06; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the keeper paddles a compact five-log raft with the crate; a big nine-log raft with the same crate drifts behind, the imp lounging on it.
